# Player DSD goldens

Independent fixtures for the bridge player's DSF and DFF demuxers (backlog
B470, PR 1b).

Generated by `scripts/player-dsd-goldens/generate.py`, which needs only the
Python standard library and writes the containers from the DSF 1.01 and
DSDIFF 1.5 specifications. Ordinary `go test` never runs that script.

To check a change to the generator without touching these files, write into
a scratch directory and point the golden tests at it:

```sh
python3 scripts/player-dsd-goldens/generate.py --out /tmp/dsd-goldens
go test -tags ts_omit_webclient,ts_omit_debugeventbus ./internal/player/decode -args -dsd-goldens=/tmp/dsd-goldens
```

The demuxer skips COMT and MANF by their sizes, so no decoding test sees
their layout: `TestDFFGoldensCOMTFollowsSection36` and
`TestDFFGoldensGiveTheWalksAnOddChunk` read the DFF files' bytes instead.

`pattern.bin` is the canonical audio every fixture carries: the left
channel's bytes, then the right channel's, `pattern_bytes_per_channel` each,
bit 7 earliest in time. A fixture with `bytes_per_channel` N carries the
first N bytes of each. No pattern byte is a bit palindrome, the two channels
differ at every index, and `0x00` never occurs, so a missed or extra bit
reversal, a channel swap, or padding read as audio each change bytes.

| File | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `lsb_dsd64_partial_block.dsf` | LSB-first DSF (each byte bit-reversed in the file), three whole 4096-byte blocks and a partial fourth whose zero padding is excluded by the sample count, an ID3 metadata chunk after the data |
| `msb_dsd128_partial_block.dsf` | MSB-first DSF passes bytes unchanged; DSD128 |
| `lsb_dsd64_whole_blocks.dsf` | Sample count ends exactly at a block boundary: EOF with no padding |
| `lsb_dsd64_797_samples.dsf` | 797 one-bit samples: 100 bytes per channel, the last carrying three bits of padding |
| `dsd64.dff` | DFF byte interleave (L, R), MSB first; FVER first (DSDIFF 1.5 §3.1); both chunk walks skip an odd chunk's pad byte before the sound data (§2.3): a 7-byte MANF in the form and the 19-byte CMPR of §3.2.3 in PROP; COMT carries its comment's pad inside its size (§3.6); DIIN and ID3 chunks after the sound data |
| `dsd256_right_first.dff` | CHNL lists SRGT before SLFT: the decoder still emits left first |
| `mono.dsf`, `six_channel.dsf`, `mono.dff`, `six_channel.dff` | Refused: `unsupported_channel_count` |
| `dst.dff` | CMPR `DST ` with a DST sound chunk: refused, `unsupported_compression`. Its CMPR ("DST Encoded") is 16 bytes, so unlike the other DFF goldens it gives PROP's walk no odd chunk; its MANF still gives the form's walk one |
